business_problem: Unipol needed a secure, scalable IT-operations foundation that could automate monitoring and incident handling, support hybrid-cloud flexibility, and serve as the platform for enterprise-wide AI adoption.
solution_summary: Unipol and IBM created NAMI, an AI-powered automation platform built on the watsonx ecosystem to modernize IT operations. IBM watsonx.ai provides the generative-AI layer and natural-language interfaces, watsonx Orchestrate supports agentic workflows, IBM Cloud Pak for Data prepares operational data, and IBM Cloud Pak for AIOps provides unified event and application visibility. The platform first ran on IBM Cloud and was later moved to a hybrid-cloud model on Red Hat OpenShift, while IBM Fusion HCI supplied the on-premises infrastructure needed to satisfy governance standards. NAMI also uses a multi-model strategy with Llama, Pixtral AI, and IBM Granite so different tasks can be matched to the right model. Together, those components integrate more than a dozen monitoring systems into a shared operational data layer where events can be analyzed, resolved, escalated, and reported with much less manual effort than before.

data_flow: Events from more than a dozen monitoring systems flow into NAMI's shared data layer through Cloud Pak for Data and Cloud Pak for AIOps, where watsonx.ai and the multi-model stack analyze them, watsonx Orchestrate coordinates actions, and the platform resolves or escalates incidents through a unified operational workflow.

business_outcome: Unipol cut event-response and incident-handling times, achieved full monitoring coverage, improved accounting and claims-processing efficiency, and created the AI-enabled operational base it plans to expand across the business.
